newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal orders evacuation on flood fears.
newsitem.headline: Nepal orders evacuation on flood fears.

text.p: KATHMANDU, June 18 ( Reuter) - The Nepali government has ordered the evacuation of 7,000 people after a warning from the meteorology department that a glacial lake in central Nepal may burst its banks, a state official said on Wednesday.
"We have instructed the district administration to carry out necessary precautionary measures," a spokesman for the Home (Interior) Ministry told Reuters.

The order followed a report of the Department Of Hydrology and Meteorology that the area covered by water in the Tsho-Rolpa glacial lake in Rolwaling Valley had increased to 1.65 sq km (0.64 sq mile) from 1.37 sq km in 1993.
"It is dangerous and may outburst in the monsoon season," glaciologist Rijan Bhakta Kayastha of the Department Of Hydrology and Meteorology, said. "The chances of the lake outburst are fifty-fifty."
Tsho-Rolpa, about 140 km (90 miles) northeast of Kathmandu close to Nepal's border with China, lies in the Gaurishankar mountain ranges at an altitude of 4,580 metres (15,026 ft).
